title: Learning classifies concurrent cardiac injury markers in cancer and COVID-19
summary: A random forest combined eight laboratory and chest-imaging measures in 201 cancer patients with COVID-19. Internal evaluation distinguished patients with troponin-defined cardiac injury, with reported AUC 0.94. Predictor timing relative to injury was not established, and outcome-informed screening preceded validation. This supports an exploratory concurrent classification result, not prediction before injury or improved patient outcomes.

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective comparison with troponin-defined injury status in 67 cases and 134 non-cases, with reported ten-fold internal validation.
evidence.unknown: Pre-injury forecasting, independent diagnostic validation and clinical benefit remain unestablished; imputation and outcome-informed feature ranking may introduce optimism.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest learns relationships between selected laboratory/imaging measurements and recorded biochemical cardiac-injury status.
